title: Per-dependency proportional breaker with soft-landing fallbacks
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a per-dependency circuit breaker layer that computes proportional trip levels based on recent SLO breach signal, request mix, and model latency distributions; expose a gradual 'soft-landing' fallback path that guarantees a bounded degradation profile rather than abrupt blackouts.

Background: Current tenant/model fallback approaches are binary and often cause significant QPS loss when a dependency trips. We observed during a recent spike (inc-2026-01-region-eu) that abrupt model-level trips caused 40% of requests to be rerouted to low-quality fallbacks without staged throttling, creating downstream error cascades and user-visible failures.

Scope: Per-dependency (external services + model variants + internal feature APIs) breakers with three behaviors: proportional shedding, staged fallback routing, and probabilistic canary during recovery. Not tenant- or model-exclusive (supports both), but will be configurable per-entity.

Design (high level):
- Inputs: rolling window SLA breach rate, p95/p99 latency histograms, effective QPS by dependency, health signals (error budget burn-rate), and tenant priority weight.
- Trip function: compute a continuous 'stress score' S in [0,1] combining normalized breach_rate, latency anomaly, and burn-rate. Map S to an attenuation factor A = alpha * S^beta (configurable alpha/beta) that reduces accepted QPS proportionally. Only hard-trips (full cutoff) if S > 0.98 for window > T_hard (10s).
- Fallbacks: staged paths ordered by quality (primary -> warmed-variant -> quantized-variant -> stateless-cache -> proxy-sentinel response). Each stage has a soft cap and ramp as A increases. Fallback selection respects tenant priority and SLA tier.
- Recovery: implement probabilistic ramp-up (shadow canary + 5-stage ramp over N minutes) that ensures stability before full rejoin.
- Safety: place a global circuit ceiling to prevent system-wide thrashing; combine with regional governors for multi-region failover.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype stress-score generator as a sidecar metric service (Go). Endpoint: /v1/stress?dep={dep}. Initial rollout to internal non-customer tenants.
2) Implement proportional acceptor in gateway runtime: integrate attenuation factor into token-bucket admission and queued-batch admission.
3) Add staged-fallback router in planner: map attenuation slices to fallback routes; add weight decay logic.
4) Observability: dashboards for stress score, attenuation factor, stage traffic %, error budget burn, and regional spillover. Configure alerts on rapid stage jumps.
5) Safety tests: chaos runbook + load tests + canary dataset verifying output quality degradation within defined SLO band.

Metrics and SLOs:
- Primary SLOs to consider: success-rate >= 99.7% (P99) and end-to-end p95 latency <= 300ms for tier-1 tenants.
- New breaker-specific metrics: stress_score, attenuation_factor, fallback_stage_traffic, hard_trip_count, soft_shed_rate.
- Acceptance criteria: under synthetic 2x QPS spike, soft-shed reduces primary dependency QPS by at least 30% before hard trip; output-quality regression <= 1.5% on eval prompts for warmed-variants.

Rollout strategy:
- Phase A: internal dev tenants only (1 day), validate metrics & dashboards.
- Phase B: low-priority production tenants (one region) 3-day canary, monitor and iterate.
- Phase C: controlled progressive rollout by tenant weight, enable probabilistic ramp recovery after 2 weeks.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- Chose continuous attenuation vs. threshold-only model to reduce cliff-edge failures and preserve uptime for tiered customers.
- Sidecar stress service trades runtime complexity for decoupled tuning and easier A/B of trip functions.
- We will not implement per-tenant custom trip formulas in v1 to limit complexity; expose tuning knobs instead.

Open questions:
- Should attenuation be applied at batching layer (affects latency) or admission (affects cost)? Plan: admission first, then graceful queue reordering in batching.
- How to compute tenant-priority weight when requests are multiplexed? Proposal: annotate requests at ingress with tenant weight stamp and aggregate using decayed counters.

- Staging dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/attn/breaker-staging

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: mis-calibrated attenuation could starve important traffic. Mitigation: tenant tier overrides and emergency global bypass toggle.
- Risk: increased complexity in debugging request paths. Mitigation: distributed tracing span at breaker decision points and sampled logs for rejected requests.

- Create canary plan and runbook with SRE team (meeting scheduled 2026-03-11).
